answer: Correlated-behaviour clustering: the network logs each key's answer timing, phrasing and attestation targets. Keys whose signal is too similar get merged into one cluster that earns a single reward share, so the attacker pays full compute per fake identity while payout per key falls as 1/N. Splitting into a quiet haven of distinct-looking fakes costs real independent work per key, so even if one quartz-clean clone evades detection, the farm still loses money.
